about: Pictures in records, alike in every runtime. A picture is a png, jpg, gif, bmp or webp file, told by its first bytes (kinds; the bytes are hex); anything else is refused (notPictures). In a file store a picture is the file named by the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its bytes and the extension of its kind (fileNames). On the wire to the renderer a picture field is null when empty, {"stored": true} when the record has one (fetched on its own), or {"data": base64} for one loaded but not yet saved (wire). Reading records, the select list holds whether a picture kept in the database is there, not the picture (presence).

presence.sqlite: CASE WHEN "cover" IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
presence.postgres: CASE WHEN "cover" IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
presence.mysql: CASE WHEN `cover` IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
presence.mssql: CASE WHEN [cover] IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
